input.quote: All minimum monthly fees (including the Monthly Base Fee) are due in advance on the first day of the calendar month in which the Services are to be performed, prorated for any partial month.
input.rationale: The Monthly Base Fee is a minimum monthly fee payable in advance for the entire eight-year Term (p0049, p0130, p0149), and Customer must source the whole bundled Service set from M&I for the Term (p0183). Nothing lets Customer reduce the minimum, and the only relief is a good-faith renegotiation if M&I itself withdraws a bundled Service (p0181). That is a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction right, i.e. walk-away territory, so we redline to the fallback: commitment limited to the current twelve-month period, reducible on thirty days' notice, with any shortfall settled by a true-up rather than a penalty. We deliberately leave the termination fee mechanics alone, as those sit under the termination-for-convenience rule.

ops.text: Minimum Commitment. Notwithstanding Section 10.3(A), Customer's commitment to any minimum monthly fee (including the Monthly Base Fee) is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period of the Term, and Customer may reduce that commitment, and the corresponding minimum monthly fees, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to M&I. Any shortfall between a minimum monthly fee and the fees for Services actually used shall be settled solely by a true-up payment of the difference, and not by any penalty.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Monthly Base Fee is an 8-year minimum with no reduction right, so we have added our fallback position: the commitment runs only for the current twelve-month period, is reducible on thirty days' notice, and any shortfall is trued up rather than penalised.
proposal.summary: Limit the minimum monthly fee commitment to the current 12-month period, allow reduction on 30 days' notice, and convert shortfall to a true-up

mappings.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
